stem: A charge nurse is making client assignments for the oncoming shift. Which information should guide the assignments?

options.A: Client acuity and needs together with each staff member's competency to perform the required care
options.B: Room location alone so assignments are geographically convenient
options.C: Client insurance status rather than clinical care needs
options.D: Staff seniority alone without considering client needs or competency

rationale: The 2026 NCSBN Test Plan directs nurses to prioritize care based on client acuity and, under Assignment, Delegation and Supervision, to assign tasks based on client needs to personnel with competency to perform them. Therefore A contains the clinically relevant assignment factors. B and C use nonclinical factors, and D ignores both client needs and staff competency.
educational_objective: Base nursing assignments on client acuity and care needs while matching required tasks to personnel who are competent to perform them.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_locator: Management of Care, printed p.7 / PDF p.11: 'Prioritize the delivery of client care based on acuity'; Appendix A, printed p.20 / PDF p.24, Assignment, Delegation and Supervision: identify tasks based on client needs and assign appropriate tasks to personnel with competency to perform tasks
source_claim_supported: Client acuity and needs, together with staff competency for required tasks, are relevant factors for prioritizing and assigning nursing care.

correction_summary: Replaced the generic claim that an 'acuity tool primarily measures complexity and intensity' with a directly NCSBN-supported nursing assignment decision. NCSBN is the required primary source for NCLEX assignment/delegation content and explicitly links prioritization to acuity and assignment to client needs and staff competency.
audit_findings: A integrates all directly supported assignment factors. B and C rely on irrelevant nonclinical criteria, while D uses seniority alone and omits client needs and competency. The item no longer depends on a proprietary or variably defined acuity-tool construct. No second answer, cueing, unsupported precision, or unresolved conflict remains.
